key_insight: Trial-level auditory oddball ERP waveforms combined with deep learning improved schizophrenia-vs-control classification compared with conventional summary-feature models.
clinical_relevance: This suggests EEG waveforms may become a useful biomarker source for supporting individual-level schizophrenia research and future decision-support tools.
method: 258 schizophrenia patients and 142 healthy controls were recorded with an auditory duration oddball EEG paradigm.
Trials were segmented into -100 to 500 ms epochs and residualized against each participant’s standard-response waveform.
Five deep learning models were compared with classical machine learning models using 18 ERP summary features.
evidence_signal: On the held-out test set, deep learning reached AUROC 0.797-0.857, outperforming feature-based models at 0.705-0.720.
watch_item: Performance was tested on one dataset with a fixed split, so external validation and real-world robustness are still needed.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Individual-Level Classification of Schizophrenia Versus Healthy Controls from Trial-Level Auditory Oddball ERP Waveforms
